articles.title: European football: PSG scramble another draw while Bayern make flying start
articles.summary: Marquinhos grabs late equaliser for Ligue 1 champions. Bayern overwhelm Stuttgart 5-1 at Allianz Arena. Paris Saint-Germain defender Marquinhos scored deep into stoppage ⁠time to snatch a scarcely deserved 2-2 draw at Lille on Friday as the Ligue 1 champions ⁠continued to struggle ⁠after ​being…
body: After the poor 2-2 draw ‌against Rennes, things went from bad to worse for PSG when Lille took the lead in the 21st minute as Icelandic playmaker Hákon Haraldsson latched on to a brilliant reverse pass from Olivier Giroud and curled an unstoppable shot past ‌Matvei Safonov.

Despite all their attacking riches, the Parisians struggled to get shots on target as Lille packed their ​defence and forced the champions to attack from wide areas, and Lille appeared to have secured the three points when Dilane Bakwa scored in the 84th minute.

PSG midfielder Vitinha threw his side ⁠a lifeline in the first minute of stoppage time with ​a superb ​strike curled into the top-left ​corner, and the Portuguese international then crossed for ​Marquinhos to head ‌home the ​equaliser four ​minutes later to complete an improbable comeback.

In the Bundesliga Bayern Munich kickstarted their title defence with a resounding 5-1 victory over Stuttgart thanks ⁠to a sparkling second-half display at the Allianz Arena that showed they have lost none of their ⁠potency from last ⁠season.

articles.title: MLB suspends Dominican prospect after age-fraud plot involving fake grave
articles.summary: Report: player posed as nearly two years younger. Scheme allegedly included fake grave and records. $2.8m agreement with Guardians was canceled. A once-prized prospect from the Dominican Republic has been suspended by Major League Baseball after a league investigation revealed the player was part…
body: The age-fraud plot included extreme efforts by the player’s handler such as falsifying school and medical records, faking birth and death certificates ⁠and even staging a gravesite, per ⁠the report.

A switch-hitting infielder ​going by the name of David Severino agreed in December to a $2.8m pre-deal with the Cleveland Guardians, who reportedly believed the player was 13 or 14 years old. The deal was ⁠set to be finalized in 2029, when Severino was expected to be 17 and eligible to officially sign.
In reality, per ESPN’s sources, Severino is 16 years old and named Daury David Severino Damaso.

In 2023, Francisco Nieves, Severino’s ⁠trainer at the time, allegedly created the false identity of David Severino Damaso, posed as Daury’s younger brother. Nieves reportedly created a false death ​certificate for Daury, claiming he died of a respiratory illness ‌two years after he was born, ‌and even built a fake tombstone that was planted at a gravesite in the Dominican Republic.

articles.title: Hovland in tie for lead at Tour Championship
articles.summary: Norway's Viktor Hovland and American Ryan Gerard in tie for the lead at 10 under, heading into the weekend at the Tour Championship in Atlanta.
body: Hovland, who was crowned the Fedex Cup champion in 2023, made a birdie on the final hole to card a four-under 66, after Gerard had set the clubhouse pace with a five-under 65.
While Hovland's putting again came to the fore, Gerard was not to be outdone and memorably rolled in a stunning 78-foot birdie putt that travelled the length of the seventh green.

Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup are joint-second on nine under, while world number one Scottie Scheffler shrugged off two early bogeys to fire a 67, leaving him just two shots back in the PGA Tour's season-ending event.
Cameron Young, who won the Players Championship in March, is also at eight under after a scintillating round of 62 that contained seven birdies and an eagle on the par-five 18th.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola tells Liverpool’s forwards to ‘exhaust themselves’
articles.summary: ‘I tell them they don’t need to give us 90 minutes’ Head coach takes charge of first home game on Saturday. Andoni Iraola has said it is more important for Liverpool’s forwards to exhaust themselves than perform for 90 minutes as he prepares to make an “emotional” Premier League bow at Anfield.
body: The Liverpool head coach hopes his attacking options will be improved by the arrival of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and another winger before Tuesday’s deadline, with only Victor Muñoz added to his front line so far. The Basque coach has outlined the demands he will put on his forwards as they adapt to a new era at Liverpool.

Iraola said: “For me, wingers, forwards, I always tell them that they don’t need to give us 90 minutes. I tell them it is good news when they are exhausted because then we have taken everything from you and someone else will come in.

“We have the situation now with Jérémy [Jacquet], who hasn’t had a proper pre-season but he is close to getting there. But normally defenders can last 90 minutes easier. For offensive players, it’s not mandatory that you play the whole game. Once you are done, we can change you. I think it’s the best way, and they all have to understand it like this.”

articles.title: St Helens playoff hopes hang by a thread after thrashing by Leeds
articles.summary: St Helens 6-34 Leeds. Rhinos return to top of table after running in six tries. If you needed any further proof that Super League’s two most successful sides are travelling in different directions in 2026, this was about as conclusive as you can get.
body: There are two very different fates awaiting Leeds Rhinos and St Helens in three weeks or so. The Rhinos will now almost certainly be resting up for a Super League playoff semi-final, having earned a bye through the opening week of the playoffs by virtue of a top-two finish. They are still favourites to end the regular season on top after this latest impressive victory.

But the Saints, barring a late miraculous run of results involving themselves and the teams around them, will be resting up and preparing for 2027, with their 60-year record of making the end-of-season playoffs ending. After back-to-back wins in the last fortnight, you wondered if this was the night that St Helens could really make people sit up and take notice.

Win here, and they would not only dent Leeds’ chances of the League Leaders’ Shield, but they would put themselves right back in the mix for the top six. Instead, what we saw was an 80 minutes very much played out to the form of 2026 on the whole. The Rhinos were impressive, Jake Connor was sensational yet again and the Saints ultimately disappointed.

If you needed any further proof that Super League’s two most successful sides are travelling in different directions in 2026, this was about as conclusive as you can get.

articles.title: A magician and a maverick - this could be Cherki's moment for Man City
articles.summary: After two goals and a swaggering display against Crystal Palace, Phil McNulty asks if this is Rayan Cherki's time to shine for Manchester City.
body: Rayan Cherki refuses to hide his emotions, an open book for all to see and hear in times of joy and disappointment.

Moments after Manchester City had put down their first heavyweight marker of the post-Pep Guardiola era by brushing aside Crystal Palace, he was asked live on TV how much he enjoyed the game. Rather than providing the usual textbook answer, he instead gave a colourfully uncomplimentary – and unprintable - description of his own first-half performance.
Erling Haaland, standing alongside Cherki as he waited to hand over the player-of-the-match award, could only laugh at the France attacker's sweary honesty.
Indeed, the 23-year-old also refuses to hide his talent, making a nonsense of his self-criticism by unveiling a Selhurst Park masterclass with two brilliant second-half goals in the 4-1 victory.

articles.title: Huddersfield upset Leigh with five-try win
articles.summary: Huddersfield Giants score five tries to upset in-form Leigh and keep the Leopards waiting to secure their place in the Super League play-offs.
body: Leigh scored the night's first try through Owen Trout but tries from Harry Rushton and Taane Milne helped put Huddersfield 14-6 ahead at half-time.
Niall Evalds extended the lead after the break before Leigh's Umyla Hanley and Huddersfield's Cole Geyer exchanged tries as the Giants remained ahead.
Robbie Mulhern's try kept Leigh alive with 11 minutes to play but Geyer's second score with six minutes remaining sealed an impressive victory for Huddersfield.

Victory for Huddersfield was their seventh of the season, with five of those victories coming in their past six matches, and moved them up to 12th in the table and above York ahead of their trip to Toulouse.

articles.title: NC State vs. UVA: What are we watching for?
articles.summary: What are the early indicators, for better or worse? These are a few. 1.) Can NC State’s defense be more consistently disruptive on passing plays? State’s defense was really, really bad on passing downs last season—its havoc rate stunk, it was bad on a per-play basis, from an EPA basis, from pretty…
body: Virginia doesn’t have a skill position group that’s scaring anybody, and as long as Beau Pribula is the starting quarterback—which I don’t think will last long—then the ceiling there is pretty low. But if he has four seconds to make a decision every time he drops back, he’s going to look like Joe Montana. The battle between UVA’s offensive line and State’s defense might be the only thing that really matters in this game.

2.) Is CJ Bailey ready to be the kind of quarterback who can carry a team to a big win? The pressure is on now. Everybody knows what kind of player Bailey is, and what he can be—and he’s being paid to deliver. Is he ready to handle it? He’s working with a brand new bunch of receivers, and he is going to have to improvise for State to have success offensively. There will be breakdowns and misunderstandings and he will need to fix a few things in the moment to keep the ball moving. It’s Week 0 and maybe the biggest game of his career so far.

articles.title: Injury uncertainty led to 'intrusive thoughts' for Alcaraz
articles.summary: Seven-time major champion Carlos Alcaraz says not knowing when he would be able to return from a wrist injury was most challenging part of his long absence.
body: Spain's Alcaraz, 23, has not played a singles match since mid-April but says he feels "great" as he prepares to make his comeback at the US Open, which begins in New York on Sunday.

Alcaraz, who beat rival Jannik Sinner in last year's final at Flushing Meadows, starts his title defence against powerful Russian Roman Safiullin in a contest which is likely to examine his lack of competitive action.
"Once I started to practice a little bit but didn't know when I'm going to [return], those thoughts were really difficult to deal with," said Alcaraz.
"I didn't know if I was going to be ready for Cincinnati, for the US Open, or [if] I'm going to miss the whole American swing.

articles.title: ‘You have to have guts to do something like this’: MLB suspends player after alleged age-scheme
articles.summary: Major League Baseball has suspended a Dominican prospect after discovering age fraud that included a fictitious death and gravesite tombstone. Back in December, the Cleveland Guardians made a $2.8 million deal with infielder David Severino, whose real name is Daury David Severino Damaso.
body: Severino, whose real age is 16, impressed scouts while competing against 12- and 13-year-olds, but speculation formed as the Dominican prospect failed to resemble his actual age.

“I had a scout tell me this Severino kid could really play,” a team executive on the international side said. “I went to see him and the first thing I thought was, ‘There’s no way this kid is the age he says he is,” Alden Gonzalez of ESPN reports.
“The face was older,” said another executive. “You could just tell he was older.”
John Pereyra, a trainer who once worked with Severino, chimed in as well.

articles.title: Greaves denied by Cross in last-leg thriller on European Tour debut
articles.summary: Beau Greaves took Rob Cross to a last-leg decider before losing out 6-5 on her European Tour debut in the first round of the Hungarian Darts Trophy.
body: Rising star Greaves, 22, made history by becoming the first woman to compete in a PDC European Tour event after qualifying last month for both this weekend's tournament in Budapest and the Czech Darts Open in September.
And she pushed the experienced Cross to a deciding 11th leg in a thrilling tie on Friday evening, averaging an impressive match-best of 104.88 and hitting five 180s.

Cross, who played well himself with an 101.90 average, had made a flying start to the match with a 170 first-leg checkout but Greaves, who is dominating the PDC women's series, quickly showed her competitiveness and took the next two legs.
She moved one more leg away from victory at 5-4 but Cross hit back to win the final two, with Greaves left to rue mistakes with her first two darts in the decider when left with 70.
